item.title: Intrabeam scattering of chirped electron bunches with non-Gaussian longitudinal distributions and slice mismatch
item.description: arXiv:2610.38268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intrabeam scattering (IBS) can significantly increase the uncorrelated energy spread of high-brightness electron bunches in linear accelerators. For chirped bunches transported through beamlines with dispersion, however, the commonly used simulation codes elegant and RF-Track give substantially different predictions. To investigate this discrepancy, a semi-analytical slice model is developed for bunches with non-Gaussian longitudinal distributions and slice-dependent transverse mismatch. The model predicts slice energy-spread evolution in beamlines with dispersion and provides an independent reference for assessing the simulation results. Benchmarks in an achromatic arc show good agreement with RF-Track for both ideal Gaussian and realistic mismatched bunches in the tested cases. The proposed model provides a practical tool for evaluating IBS in linacs beyond the ideal-Gaussian approximation. The comparison also suggests directions for improving the accuracy and efficiency of PIC-based IBS simulations.
item.dc:creator: Xiuji Chen, Wencai Cheng, Si Chen, Duan Gu, Haixiao Deng

item.title: Bayesian optimization of longitudinally aligned CNT targets for 800 nm laser wakefield acceleration in the bubble regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.38810v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Laser wakefield acceleration (LWFA) in solid-density plasmas can reach accelerating gradients in the TeV/m range, well above those of gaseous media, provided the driver is matched to the plasma. In nanostructured solids, this matching can be achieved by controlling the spacing between the nanostructures to reduce the effective density, enabling infrared pulses to excite wakefields in the bubble regime. Following numerical demonstrations with carbon nanotube (CNT) bundles on concentric cylindrical shells, a simpler, experimentally more accessible longitudinally aligned CNT (LA-CNT) target is investigated here, with the bundles on a triangular lattice within a square cross section and an optional central aperture. Three-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations are coupled with Bayesian optimization to vary the effective density, target length, bundle radius and aperture radius for a fixed 100 mJ, few-cycle, 800 nm laser pulse, maximizing the laser-to-beam energy conversion efficiency for electrons above 20 MeV. With the aperture radius constrained to at least 0.5 $\mu$m, the best target operates in the bubble regime and reaches an efficiency of 24.6%, delivering a 673 pC bunch with a mean energy of 36.6 MeV and a quasi-monoenergetic peak near 46 MeV, against 19% for the concentric-shell target under identical conditions. When the aperture is allowed to vanish, the optimization converges to denser and shorter targets, the efficiency peaks at 25.8%, and the best configurations deliver a higher charge at the cost of a lower peak energy and about 50% larger divergence; aperture-free targets among them retain a mean efficiency of 24.1%. The optimized targets are robust to random bundle displacements that preserve the effective density. By eliminating the need to pattern a micrometre-scale opening, aperture-free targets may facilitate proof-of-principle experiments on solid-state LWFA.

item.title: FCC-\mu e: High Energy, High Luminosity Muon-Electron Collider & Neutrino Factory at CERN
item.description: arXiv:2610.40451v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The concept is presented of making at the FCC-$ee$ (or CEPC) facility $\mu^+e^-$ collisions at the centre-of-mass energy between 1 and 2 TeV and the average luminosity above $10^{34}$cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, concurrently to the $e^+e^-$ collisions. First, a concise scientific motivation is given, including the exciting prospect of measurements of the Higgs boson self-interaction, and is followed by a presentation of the FCC-$\mu e$ layout -- from the source of ultra-cold anti-muons, through the muon booster, to the main muon ring. Basic considerations are also given regarding the machine-detector interface and the performance of the FCC-$\mu e$ and associated neutrino factory. The paper concludes with an outlook underlying relevance of such anti-muon beams for any future high energy storage ring as well as for neutrino science.
item.dc:creator: K. Piotrzkowski

item.title: Phase-Space Shaping due to Betatron Cooling in Wakefield Accelerators and the Onset of the Ion-Channel Laser
item.description: arXiv:2510.24567v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Plasma-based accelerators are beginning to employ relativistic beams with unprecedented charge and ultrashort durations. These dense driver beams can drive wakes even in high-density plasmas ($\gtrsim10^{19}$ cm$^{-3}$), where betatron radiation becomes increasingly important and begins to affect the dynamics of the accelerated beam. We show that betatron cooling leads to a strong structuring of the phase space of the beam. This gives rise to bunched, ring-like structures with positive radial position and momentum gradients, \emph{i.e.}, population inversion of the amplitude of oscillation. We derive the characteristic timescales for this process analytically and confirm our predictions with multi-dimensional Particle-in-Cell simulations. The radiation-dominated regime of beam dynamics fundamentally alters the acceleration process and produces self-structured beams\reviewtwo{; Particle-in-Cell simulations of the resulting beams show that it becomes unstable to the ion-channel laser and lead to exponential amplification of radiation.
item.dc:creator: Pablo J. Bilbao, Thales Silva, Luis O. Silva

item.title: Brilliance: toward autonomous computational research in particle accelerator physics
item.description: arXiv:2610.15615v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Computational research in physics requires continuous interplay between simulation and scientific interpretation, demanding substantial specialist effort. Here we introduce Brilliance, a research agent that combines large language models, reusable physics knowledge and numerical simulation to conduct adaptive investigations in accelerator physics. Given a single user prompt, Brilliance designs a fourth-generation synchrotron light source that meets coupled emittance and nonlinear-acceptance requirements. Further exploration yields a design combining sub-10-pm emittance with a large dynamic aperture under realistic engineering constraints, suggesting a route towards hard-X-ray diffraction-limited operation, although the momentum-acceptance target remains unmet. Brilliance also calibrates a model of an operating light source against measured responses, accurately inferring its lattice and calibration errors. Across these studies, Brilliance autonomously revises its computational strategies in response to numerical evidence. These results demonstrate a route towards delegating sustained scientific investigations to agents equipped with domain expertise and numerical tools.
item.dc:creator: Jinyu Wan, Yu Zhao, Wei Bao, Ying Li, Hao Zhong, Xiaohan Lu, Yi Jiao
